title: P2.10a Resolve Gate 1 from authenticated durable human authority
description: Prerequisite for Product Contract Gate 1. Current core-only code exports a caller-callable gate factory and grantHumanAuthority; the latter accepts a structural HUMAN principal and caller time, while production consumer/writer grep is empty. Build or compose a daemon-owned authenticated-session approval command plus durable reader so Gate 1 can only be satisfied from a server-resolved, work-bound record. Until that exists, consumers must receive a stable UNATTESTED refusal; never synthesize a principal, signer, timestamp, or positive fixture.
definitionOfDone: Verify-or-block at current HEAD: enumerate every production authenticated human session source, approval writer, durable store record, and Gate 1 consumer. If no provenance-preserving composition is buildable, preserve UNATTESTED and report the exact missing producer rather than inventing one.

A daemon-owned command derives principal identity and time from authenticated server context, binds the approval to exact contractId/revisionId/revisionDigest/workRef, persists it durably, and refuses caller-supplied principal kind/id/time or grant bytes with exact stable code and layer.

A production Gate 1 reader resolves the durable record by exact work identity, verifies integrity/replay/staleness/foreign-work/transplant boundaries, and is composed by a real consumer; the core helper alone is not proof and no caller can invoke a public minter to satisfy the gate.

Focused daemon/core/consumer tests run with nonzero counts and assert missing, forged caller, agent-authored, stale, replayed, foreign-work, transplanted, and mutated-store refusals. Caller-forgery, authority-bypass, and production-writer-removal mutations each redden the named exact-code/layer assertion; broader gates are path-attributed.
taskRails: Human authority is not delegable: never synthesize principal, signer, custody, timestamp, approval, waiver, or activation authority.
Re-measure production writers/readers and existing authentication/session authority before planning; do not treat structural core helpers or test fixtures as production proof.
Preserve foreign WIP and commit explicit owned paths only; stable UNATTESTED is the required result while authority is absent.

TDD RED — the durable Gate 1 approval reader. All arms in a NEW file apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-reader.test.ts. Every arm RED for its stated reason before any production byte; quote the red in the step note.

DRIVE THE WRITER THROUGH PRODUCTION, NEVER A FIXTURE. Mirror product-contract-gate-1-command.test.ts:1-150 exactly: `SqliteEventStore.openForProject`, `installTestRecoveryBinding`, `createSessionAuthority` to mint a REAL HUMAN session and a REAL AGENT session, then `createStoreDependencies` + `handleCommandRequest` to submit `product_contract.approve_gate_1`. That harness is why the HUMAN/AGENT split under test is the one `sessions.authenticate` actually reports. Do not hand-assemble an approval record, a grant, a principal or a moment.

THE TRIPLE MUST BE A REAL ONE. Unlike the command's suite, which uses an arbitrary `"ab".repeat(32)` digest, this row must first `commitProductContractRevision(store, {draft})` and take the returned `ref` — the approval's revisionDigest has to be the digest of a revision that actually exists, or the resolver's positive arm is untestable.

ARMS, each asserting the EXACT code AND the refusing layer, never merely "refused":
(1) ABSENT — no approval at the work identity.
(2) EVENT_UNEXPECTED — a foreign event type committed at the Gate 1 aggregate address.
(3) SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED — a wrong `domainSchemaVersion` on an otherwise well-formed event.
(4) RECORD_MALFORMED — payload bytes that are not the exact stored key roster {contractId, gateId, grant, revisionDigest, revisionId, workRef}.
(5) TRANSPLANT / MUTATED STORE — a well-formed record whose OWN `workRef` differs from the work identity its aggregate address encodes. THIS IS THE ROW'S ONLY NON-VACUOUS TRANSPLANT FIXTURE; see step 6.
(6) FOREIGN WORK — an approval written for revision A, read at revision B's work identity, answers ABSENT (different aggregate) and never A's record.
(7) DURABLE_STORE passthrough — a throwing `readEvents` surfaces the store's own code under the DURABLE_STORE layer, not a local restatement.
(8) POSITIVE — a lawfully written HUMAN approval reads back with its stored triple and gate.
(9) AGENT — an AGENT-authored attempt never produces a readable approval, because core's `grantHumanAuthority` refused the write.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN — the reader. NEW files apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-reader.ts and its bridge product-contract-gate-1-reader.js. Target under 250 lines; the two landed siblings are 106 and 145.

THE .js BRIDGE IS MANDATORY AND INVISIBLE TO BOTH tsc AND vitest — a missing one reds unrelated files at runtime. Its entire content is one line, exactly as product-contract-revision-reader.js: `export * from "./product-contract-gate-1-reader.ts";`

`readProductContractGate1Approval(store, { projectId, ref })`:
(a) WORK IDENTITY IS NEVER SPELLED LOCALLY. `const gate = productContractGate1Authority(ref)` from @moe/core, then `deriveProductContractGate1AggregateId(gate.workRef)` from ./product-contract-gate-1-contract.js. Reconstructing either string by hand is the one way a transplant can be arranged from outside — core's own comment says so.
(b) `store.readEvents(aggregateId)` inside try/catch; `DurableStoreError` forwards its code under the DURABLE_STORE layer, anything else becomes a `STORAGE_DEGRADED` runtime error. Copy the shape of product-contract-revision-reader.ts:80-88 rather than inventing a second convention.
(c) Refuse in this order, each with its own exact code: zero events ABSENT, more than one AMBIGUOUS, wrong eventType EVENT_UNEXPECTED, wrong domainSchemaVersion SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, payload not the exact key roster RECORD_MALFORMED, record.workRef !== gate.workRef WORK_IDENTITY_MISMATCH.
(d) Return the decoded approval: the stored triple and the stored gate, frozen.

TWO TRAPS, both measured and recorded in comment-8ad30fd047b84f859ed4bbb2dfbbaaaf. FIRST: `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_CODES` in -contract.ts is documented CLOSED and "exactly the codes THIS module emits" — declare a SEPARATE closed union here; do not extend it, or one refusal gains two spellings and the layer that answered stops being legible. SECOND: a column-zero exported `*_LAYER` const enrolls the file in tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts, an explicitly enumerated list with a rotated count. Keep the layer constant module-private and export only the closed TYPE, exactly as product-contract-revision-reader.ts:22 does.

TDD RED — the resolver. All arms in a NEW file apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-resolver.test.ts, driven through the same production harness as step 2.

THE POSITIVE ARM IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE ROW AND IT MUST BE HONEST: commit a real revision with `commitProductContractRevision`, submit `product_contract.approve_gate_1` over THAT ref through `handleCommandRequest` on a real HUMAN session, then resolve. Nothing in the arm may hand-build a revision, a digest, a grant or a gate. If you find yourself constructing any of those four, stop — that is the exact fabrication this row exists to prevent, and it is a block, not a workaround.

ARMS, each pinning the exact code AND the refusing layer:
(1) SATISFIED — the lawful composition answers with core's own GATE_1 verdict object, forwarded verbatim.
(2) NO APPROVAL — a revision exists, no grant does; the reader's ABSENT code and layer travel out unchanged.
(3) NO DURABLE REVISION — an approval whose triple names a revision never committed; the revision reader's PRODUCT_CONTRACT_REVISION_ABSENT and its layer travel out unchanged.
(4) AGENT-AUTHORED — no satisfying path exists, and the refusal is core's, from `grantHumanAuthority`, not a daemon restatement.
(5) FORGED CALLER — a caller-supplied gate, grant, principal or moment cannot reach the verdict at all, because the resolver reads its gate from the STORE and takes no gate parameter. Assert the signature makes this unrepresentable rather than asserting a runtime rejection of it.
(6) TRANSPLANTED — the mutated-store record from step 2 arm (5) refuses at the reader's layer and never reaches core.
(7) STALENESS / GRANT-INTERNAL DEFECTS — assert core's `checkHumanAuthority` code and layer arrive VERBATIM. The resolver must add no second adjudication; collapsing a grant-internal defect into a local GATE_1 code is indistinguishable from not detecting it, which is core's own documented reason at product-contract-acceptance-binding.ts:87-92.

GREEN — the resolver. NEW files apps/daemon/src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-resolver.ts and its one-line bridge product-contract-gate-1-resolver.js (`export * from "./product-contract-gate-1-resolver.ts";`). Target under 250 lines.

`resolveProductContractGate1(store, { projectId, ref })`, composition only:
(a) `readProductContractGate1Approval` — refusal forwarded VERBATIM, its code and layer untouched.
(b) `readProductContractRevision(store, { projectId, ref: <the APPROVAL's stored triple> })` — note the ref comes from the DURABLE APPROVAL, not from the caller; that is what makes the answer caller-independent. Refusal forwarded VERBATIM.
(c) `validateProductContractGate1(<the durable revision>, <the stored gate>)` — returned VERBATIM, refusal or verdict.

TAKE NO GATE PARAMETER AND EXPOSE NO MINTER PATH. The function's only inputs are a store, a project id and a revision ref. A caller cannot present a gate, a grant, a principal or a time, so DoD 3's "no caller can invoke a public minter to satisfy the gate" is enforced by the SIGNATURE, not by a runtime check that a future refactor could relax.

DO NOT RE-DERIVE THE CONTENT DIGEST HERE, and do not re-compare the durable revision's triple to the approval's. Both are already answered upstream and a restatement is a vacuous guard: `readProductContractRevision` refuses PRODUCT_CONTRACT_REVISION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH when the decoded triple differs from the requested ref (product-contract-revision-reader.ts:66-72), and core re-verifies the CONTENT digest inside `admitProductContractRevision` (product-contract-codec.ts:120) on the path `validateProductContractGate1` -> `admittedRevision`. A third copy would trip on the same inputs as those two and prove nothing. If you believe a divergence input exists that only a local check can catch, that is a FINDING to write up with the input — not a guard to add on suspicion.

Closed code roster and module-private layer, same two traps as step 3.

MUTATION DRILLS (DoD 4), each alone, ONE degree of freedom at a time. Back both production modules up to Windows %TEMP% (never MSYS /tmp) suffixed by your worker id BEFORE the first mutation; prove each restore by SHA256 equality against that backup in a call SEPARATE from the restore — a PowerShell copy can silently no-op, and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. Both files are NEW and therefore UNTRACKED (`??`), so `git diff` is blind to them and is NOT a valid restore proof here. Confirm each mutation actually LANDED on disk before re-running.

D1 CALLER-FORGERY — widen the resolver to accept a caller-supplied gate and prefer it over the stored one. EXPECTED: step 4 arm (5) reds. If the arm cannot red because it only asserts a type, replace it with one that can: this is the drill that proves the signature is load-bearing.
D2 AUTHORITY-BYPASS — make the resolver return a satisfied verdict without calling `validateProductContractGate1`. EXPECTED: the AGENT-authored and grant-internal arms red on their exact CORE codes, not on a local one.
D3 PRODUCTION-WRITER-REMOVAL — make `readProductContractRevision` unreachable from the resolver (return the approval alone). EXPECTED: step 4 arm (3) reds with PRODUCT_CONTRACT_REVISION_ABSENT missing. This is the drill that proves the row actually resolves a DURABLE revision rather than trusting the approval's triple, which is the exact clause comment-e18313bef3e343ef9432ac0b9c702265 left open.

DIVERGENCE FENCE (epic rail 7A) — read this before banking the transplant arm. The reader's `record.workRef !== gate.workRef` check can only be exercised by a MUTATED STORE, because the writer derives both sides from the same gate object and no lawful input diverges them. Step 2 arm (5) is therefore the arm that keeps it honest, and D4 proves it: DELETE that check and confirm arm (5) reds. If it stays GREEN the check is unreachable as written — report it as a FINDING with the input you tried, and never respond by deleting the surviving assertion.

A drill that comes back GREEN is a FINDING to report in a comment, never a pass to bank.

GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, DURABLE RECORD, PATHSPEC COMMIT. Each leg FOREGROUND, UNPIPED, ALONE. A piped run reports tail's exit code; a `;` chain reports only the last command's. An exit-0 leg printing no count line executed NOTHING and is UNVERIFIED, not passing.

LEG A: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-reader.test.ts src/product-contract/product-contract-gate-1-resolver.test.ts` — exit 0; quote the `Test Files` and `Tests` count lines.

LEG C: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` — exit 0; quote the `$ tsc` echo as execution evidence and compare against step 1(e)'s pre-edit baseline. If it returns sub-second, plant one type error in the resolver as a positive control, confirm red, remove it, prove the removal by SHA256 against your %TEMP% backup in a separate call.
LEG D: `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` — exit 0 with counts. This row adds no core byte, so a core red is foreign; run it to attribute, not to fix.
Repo-wide red is PATH-ATTRIBUTED: record failures at merge-base and at HEAD and report the (HEAD minus merge-base) set intersected with this row's owned paths. Completion needs that intersection EMPTY, with foreign red disclosed verbatim — never hidden, never fabricated green.
